newsitem.title: USA: L.A. redevelopment agency cuts staff, budget-paper.
newsitem.headline: L.A. redevelopment agency cuts staff, budget-paper.

text.p: The Los Angeles Community Redevelopment Agency has cut its staff and budget and put projects on hold because of stagnant real estate values, according to a published report on Wednesday.

Facing what may be its worst financial crisis in its 49-year history, the agency has laid off 23 workers, slashed its budget by 27 percent over the last three years and put off work on several new projects, the Los Angeles Times reported.
"Our property taxes have bottomed out," John Molloy, the agency's executive administrator, told the Times. "We are in the trough."
The Times said the city council would consider a motion Wednesday to provide the agency some relief by putting off a plan to divert $4.5 million from the agency's budget to the city general fund.
